title: The only true thing in life?
html_source:
Recall what Cranly said to Stephen in A Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man:

Whatever else is unsure in this stinking dunghill of a world a mother’s love is not.

anchor.text: The only true thing in life?
anchor.prefix: eart. But for her the race of the world would have trampled him underfoot, a squashed boneless snail. She had loved his weak watery blood drained from her own. Was that then real?
anchor.suffix: His mother's prostrate body the fiery Columbanus in holy zeal bestrode. She was no more: the trembling skeleton of a twig burnt in the fire, an odour of rosewood and wetted ashes.
anchor.canonical_text: The only true thing in life?
